findings.borderlineResolution: Held at Low. Flag for explicit human decision before story-103 broadcast.

analysis.assetRisk: None. Gate reverts before any value moves; abort() returns all four handled tokens to the old pooler (fork-proven incl. paused pool/vault). Tax/accounting constraint (052 L23) is also preserved: abort is contract-to-contract.
analysis.attackPath: Concrete and permissionless: sUSDS.transfer(pair,1)+sync() between createPair and exitAndSeed. No hypotheticals. Permanence for THIS escrow (and any redeploy of the same bytecode) is real: synced reserves with totalSupply 0 cannot be returned to (0,0).
analysis.conditions: Attacker-controlled only (watch for createPair in a multi-tx --slow broadcast). Not an external precondition; does not by itself cap severity.
analysis.impact: Availability of a not-yet-executed, one-off, fully reversible operator migration. No user-facing or ongoing protocol function is impaired: old pooler continues operating after abort, UniPoolerV2/canonical pair remain seedable via transfer+pair.mint (fork-proven). Cost to protocol = delay + writing/reviewing a mint-path seeder.

findings.law1Consideration: Holding at Low does not leave a live exploit: the failure mode is fail-safe (revert -> abort -> status quo). The Law-1 obligations here are recall and visibility, both satisfied: the finding is open, not suppressed under L-24, and discloses why L-24's recovery premise does not hold in this contract. The one genuinely Law-1-adjacent risk is secondary: a rushed post-brick replacement seeder doing router addLiquidity with zero/loose mins into a skewed pair (the exact anti-pattern L-24's triageReason forbids). That is addressed by pre-broadcast mitigation, not by inflating this label.
findings.whyNotMedium: C4 Medium's availability prong targets impaired protocol function. Three independent facts keep this out: (1) zero asset risk, (2) zero users or ongoing protocol functions affected, (3) full status-quo restore via a permissioned, fork-proven abort. A DoS of a migration helper that is fixed by deploying a different helper is delay, not availability loss. Consistent with precedents L-24 (owner wont-fix, same primitive) and phStaging run-39 L-01 (Low). This is not a genuinely 50/50 call, so the keep-the-higher-severity tie-break does not apply.
upgradeTriggers: If the cutover acquires real time pressure where delay itself exposes assets (e.g. funds left in a Balancer pool known to be at risk, or a hard deadline after which the Proportional/Recovery exit is unavailable and value is lost), re-weigh to Medium.
If a replacement path is shown to be unavailable (e.g. tax/accounting constraint forbids any other seeder contract), re-weigh: the cutover would then be permanently blockable.
findings.notes: Agree with classifier and validity checker. The borderline flag is honest and should stay in the write-up so the human decides knowingly whether to re-apply L-24's wont-fix.
corrections: Title/failure step 2: the 'dust pair.mint' variant is not ~1 wei. A first mint on an empty pair requires sqrt(a*b) > MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY (1000), i.e. on the order of 1,001 wei per side. Still negligible; say '~1 wei (sync) or ~1e3 wei per side (mint) + gas'.

Recommended mitigation should be framed as a pre-broadcast decision for story-103/108: either add the mint-path branch now, or document the abort + mint-path-seeder runbook (with reserve-ratio assertion, never zero-min router addLiquidity into a skewed pair) before broadcast, so recovery is not improvised under pressure.

analysis.assetRisk: Real, permanent stranding of whatever new-pool token X the owner sends via withdrawBPT after setPool(X). Original BPT is never at risk.
analysis.attackPath: No attacker. Owner sequence setPool(X) -> withdrawBPT(escrow, n), fork-proven.
analysis.conditions: Two owner calls not present in story-103; story-052 L208 puts escrow deploy and withdrawBPT in the same broadcast. Realistic window is escrow re-use after an abort followed by a repoint.
analysis.impact: Permanent loss of owner-sent assets through a non-obvious interaction (abort() is documented as the universal undo).

findings.notes: Do not downgrade to QA. Both Low and QA are defensible, and the consequence (permanent, unrescuable loss of real assets) is exactly the non-obvious Law-3 footgun class that stays in scope at honest severity; the symmetry rule keeps the higher label. Not Medium: owner-only path, not on the runbook, low likelihood.
corrections: Adopt validity-checker corrections: cite story-052 L345 (no-rescue for non-handled tokens is accepted INFO) and explain the difference (token arrives via the protocol's own withdrawBPT, not an airdrop).
Cite story-052 L208 when stating likelihood; state the realistic window as escrow re-use after an abort (e.g. forced by L-26 or L-28) plus a repoint.
Cross-reference L-26/L-28: an abort-and-reuse scenario is exactly what those findings make likely, which is the main path to this footgun.

Both Low and QA defensible; keep Low per the symmetry rule. Not Medium: temporary and operator-mitigable.
